_doc: Shared discovery-parity scenarios, run against BOTH discovery walkers: the native `tsv_cli::cli::discover::discover_files` (tests/discovery_parity.rs) and the WASM `cli.js` (scripts/test_npm.ts). One source of truth so the two implementations can't drift. The matcher itself is checked against real `git check-ignore` by tsv_ignore's git_oracle; this table pins the WALK (repo-root detection, hierarchical layering, the build-output heuristic, the scope of a named path, argument rejection, the .git boundary). Each scenario materializes `tree` in a fresh tempdir (string value = file, null = empty directory; `.git`/`repo/.git` entries make a dir look like a repo root without a real git binary), then for every case runs `format --list <root>/<target>`. A case carries EITHER `expected` — the in-scope files, relative to the tempdir root, in exact sorted order — OR `error`, a substring of the argument error that must fail the run upfront (exit 2, nothing listed). An `expected` case may add `warns`: substrings each of which some warning the walk emits must carry, and `no_warns`: substrings no warning may carry (exit code and stdout untouched either way) — the one pin on the warnings channel as a walk PRODUCT, where the texts themselves are tsv_discover's unit tests'. A tree value may also be `{"symlink": "<target>"}`, a symbolic link to `<target>` resolved from the link's own directory; a scenario holding one needs unix, and both harnesses skip it elsewhere. Names are ASCII so Rust's PathBuf order and cli.js's compare_paths agree (see cli.js compare_paths for the astral-plane/Windows caveat).

scenarios.name: respects_prettierignore
scenarios.note: repo-root .prettierignore (no .formatignore to shadow it) prunes a dir + a glob

scenarios.name: formatignore_shadows_prettierignore
scenarios.note: in a repo, a repo-root .formatignore is used ALONE — the repo-root .prettierignore is not read, so its pattern has no effect (p_only.ts stays in scope) — and the shadow is warned about whether the shadowing directory is walked (target `.`) or only preloaded as an ancestor (target `sub`)

scenarios.name: gitignore_prunes_and_heuristic_off
scenarios.note: a .gitignore is authoritative: gitignored dist/ is pruned, but a non-gitignored build/ (which the old heuristic wrongly skipped) is in scope

scenarios.name: nested_gitignore_reinclude
scenarios.note: root ignores *.gen.ts; a deeper .gitignore re-includes one file (git's deeper-wins)

scenarios.name: subdir_target_finds_repo_root_ignores
scenarios.note: targeting a subdir still walks up to the repo-root .git and applies the repo-root .gitignore AND .formatignore

scenarios.name: git_repo_without_gitignore_keeps_heuristic
scenarios.note: a repo with no .gitignore keeps the heuristic on — dist/ stays skipped

scenarios.name: nested_gitignore_disables_heuristic_in_subtree
scenarios.note: no root .gitignore keeps the heuristic on (root dist/ pruned), but a nested pkg/.gitignore — even empty — turns it off for pkg's subtree, so pkg/dist/ (which the heuristic would skip) is formatted. Pins the heuristic-active threading at depth (a nested .gitignore disabling the heuristic only for its own subtree)

scenarios.name: formatignore_reincludes_gitignored_file
scenarios.note: the tsv layer is applied after .gitignore, so a .formatignore `!` re-includes a file-level gitignore exclusion

scenarios.name: skips_other_vcs_dirs
scenarios.note: .hg/.svn/.jj/.sl (Sapling — prettier parity) are safety nets, pruned even in a git tree whose authoritative .gitignore (heuristic off) doesn't mention them

scenarios.name: explicit_file_is_bounded_by_the_ignore_files
scenarios.note: a named FILE is bounded by the ignore files as the walk that reaches it is: one a rule excludes — itself, or through an ancestor directory — is skipped, and one no rule excludes is in scope. A .prettierignore (or .formatignore) rule's skip is quiet; a .gitignore rule's warns with the exact lines that re-include the file, for the file the repo root reads — here its .prettierignore, since a .formatignore created beside it would shadow every rule in it

warns: gen/g.ts is inside gen, which a rule in the repo-root .gitignore excludes, so it is not formatted; re-include it by adding `!/gen/`, `/gen/*` and `!/gen/g.ts`, in that order, to the repo-root .prettierignore

scenarios.name: explicit_dir_a_tsv_rule_excludes_names_the_rules_file
scenarios.note: a named DIRECTORY a .formatignore or .prettierignore rule excludes warns, naming the file the rule sits in — a nested .prettierignore by its repo-relative path — while a named FILE the same rule excludes is skipped quietly

warns: pkg/gen is excluded by a rule in pkg/.prettierignore, so nothing under it is formatted; narrow or negate that rule to format it

scenarios.name: explicit_path_reads_no_ignore_file_inside_an_excluded_directory
scenarios.note: a named path reads no ignore file inside a directory a rule excludes, as the walk that prunes the directory reads none: a named file there is skipped quietly despite the .prettierignore its directory's .formatignore shadows, and a named directory under it warns only that it is excluded

warns: vendor/sub is inside vendor, which a rule in the repo-root .formatignore excludes, so nothing under it is formatted; narrow or negate that rule to format it

scenarios.name: explicit_path_a_tsv_rule_also_excludes_names_that_rule
scenarios.note: a .formatignore rule excluding a named path is the one reported even where a .gitignore excludes the path first — re-including past the .gitignore would leave that rule standing, and, added to the same file, override it: a file it excludes is skipped quietly, a directory names it, and a path only the .gitignore excludes still gets the lines that re-include it

warns: vendor/lib is excluded by a rule in the repo-root .formatignore, so nothing under it is formatted; narrow or negate that rule to format it

vendor/y.ts is inside vendor, which a rule in the repo-root .gitignore excludes, so it is not formatted; re-include it by adding `!/vendor/`, `/vendor/*` and `!/vendor/y.ts`, in that order, to the repo-root .formatignore

scenarios.name: explicit_file_does_not_bypass_the_extension
scenarios.note: a named FILE is checked for its extension before anything else: an unsupported one is an argument error, because the parser dispatch behind a path has no unknown arm (everything that isn't .svelte/.css goes to the TypeScript parser) — a named .json would be parsed as TS, and a top-level-array one silently rewritten into invalid JSON. A DIRECTORY arg is a scope rather than a target, so the same files inside it are simply filtered out by the walk

scenarios.name: list_in_scope_honors_ignores
scenarios.note: the in-scope set honors a dir prune (build/) and a glob (*.snap)

scenarios.name: fully_ignored_target_is_empty
scenarios.note: a target under an ignored dir discovers nothing (empty scope is valid) — both the dir itself and a deeper subdir — and warns, naming the kind of file whose rule excluded it and the remedy that kind takes. The walk's per-entry matcher query is leaf-only (no ancestor prune), so this pins the root-gate that re-applies the full ancestor walk to the named root, one and two levels deep

warns: build is excluded by a rule in the repo-root .gitignore, so nothing under it is formatted; re-include it by adding `!/build/` to the repo-root .formatignore

build/sub is inside build, which a rule in the repo-root .gitignore excludes, so nothing under it is formatted; re-include it by adding `!/build/`, `/build/*` and `!/build/sub/`, in that order, to the repo-root .formatignore

scenarios.name: sort_is_component_wise_at_separator_boundary
scenarios.note: output is ordered component-wise (the separator sorts before other bytes), so `a/`'s file precedes `a-b/`'s even though '-' < '/' in plain byte order. Native PathBuf order and cli.js compare_paths agree; the native sort key (path_sort_key) must preserve it

scenarios.name: cwd_independent_decision
scenarios.note: a non-repo project's own .formatignore prunes gen/ (gen/ is not a heuristic dir, so the ignore file is the only thing that can skip it)

scenarios.name: subtree_consistent_direct_vs_via_root
scenarios.note: targeting a subdir directly vs via the repo root yields the same decisions for that subdir — the repo-root .gitignore applies either way

scenarios.name: reinclude_overrides_heuristic
scenarios.note: with no .gitignore the build/dist/target heuristic is on, but an explicit .formatignore `!build/` re-includes the dir over the guess

scenarios.name: formatignore_is_hierarchical
scenarios.note: a nested .formatignore governs its subtree; a deeper `!` re-includes

scenarios.name: prettierignore_is_hierarchical
scenarios.note: a nested .prettierignore governs its subtree, like .formatignore (both are hierarchical tsv layers); the repo-root one applies too, and a subdir invocation still walks up to the .git root and picks up the nested one

scenarios.name: prettierignore_shadow_is_per_directory
scenarios.note: a directory's .formatignore shadows only its OWN sibling .prettierignore (per-directory); a .prettierignore in another directory is unaffected and still applies (a/.formatignore does not disable b/.prettierignore)

scenarios.name: prettierignore_deeper_reincludes
scenarios.note: hierarchical .prettierignore layers are last-match-wins by depth like .formatignore: a deeper .prettierignore `!` re-includes a file a shallower tsv layer ignored

scenarios.name: no_borrowed_ignores_outside_repo
scenarios.note: outside a repo, neither .prettierignore nor .gitignore is consulted; only the native .formatignore governs

scenarios.name: git_boundary_blocks_ancestor_formatignore
scenarios.note: the .git boundary is the hard stop: an ancestor .formatignore ABOVE the repo must not reach inside it

scenarios.name: ancestor_formatignore_applies_outside_repo
scenarios.note: outside any repo, an ancestor .formatignore governs descendants (filesystem-as-API / global config): a named file it excludes is skipped quietly, and a named directory it excludes warns, naming the .formatignore by its absolute path

warns: .formatignore, so nothing under it is formatted; narrow or negate that rule to format it

scenarios.name: explicit_subdir_under_a_built_in_prune_is_in_scope
scenarios.note: the safety nets and the build-output heuristic prune only what a walk DISCOVERS: a named directory is never pruned by them, neither at itself nor through an ancestor, so a subdirectory of a heuristic dir (no .gitignore, so dist/ is guessed build output), of a safety net (node_modules/) or of a hidden dir lists what naming its parent lists for it — and warns about nothing, since no rule the user wrote is involved. Walking down from the repo root still prunes all three, and a walk below a named root still prunes its own children (dist/sub/build/)

scenarios.name: pruned_ancestor_outside_repo_is_not_graded
scenarios.note: outside a git repo as inside one, the safety nets and the heuristic do not grade a named subdirectory's ANCESTORS (they grade no named path): a loose project under a heuristic or hidden directory (a /build sandbox, ~/.cache) stays in scope. Walking down from the tempdir root still prunes those directories (no .gitignore is read outside a repo, so the heuristic is on)

scenarios.name: a_directory_named_like_an_ignore_file_is_not_one
scenarios.note: an ignore file is present when it is a REGULAR file, by the same rule whether its directory is walked or only preloaded as an ancestor: a directory named .formatignore does not shadow the sibling .prettierignore, and a directory named .gitignore neither turns the heuristic off nor warns about a file it could not read

scenarios.name: a_symlinked_ignore_file_is_followed
scenarios.note: an ignore file reached through a symlink is read, by the same rule whether its directory is walked or only preloaded (a listing's own file type does not follow the link, so the walk has to)

scenarios.name: a_symlinked_gitignore_is_not_applied
scenarios.note: git does not follow a symbolic link to a .gitignore in a working tree (gitignore(5)) — it warns and applies none of the linked rules — so neither does tsv, by the same rule whether the directory is walked or only preloaded: g.ts stays in scope at both depths, and with no .gitignore applied the build-output heuristic stays on and prunes dist/, which a regular .gitignore would have turned off. The tsv layer keeps following links (the scenario above)

warns: sub/.gitignore is a symbolic link, which git does not follow
sub/.gitignore is a symbolic link, which git does not follow

scenarios.name: heuristic_shadow_warning_names_the_rules_file
scenarios.note: the build-output heuristic prunes a dist/ that a tsv-layer `!` re-include was written under, and the warning names the file holding that rule, with the directory re-include spelled for that file — anchored and relative to its directory, since a repo-root-relative `!pkg/dist/` pasted into pkg/.formatignore is anchored to pkg and does nothing. Applied (fix/.prettierignore), the anchored lines admit fix/dist and select keep.ts in it, while fix/sub/dist — which an unanchored `!dist/` would re-include too — stays pruned, and unwarned

warns: pkg/dist is skipped by tsv's build-output heuristic, so a re-include under it in pkg/.formatignore does nothing; re-include the directory itself there with `!/dist/` (then `/dist/*` + `!/dist/<file>` to select files within it)
pkg/dist is skipped by tsv's build-output heuristic, so a re-include under it in pkg/.formatignore
